context:
SITE & AUDIENCE
- utilityexplained.com — Hugo static site explaining utility bills (electricity/gas/water) to ordinary US consumers. Revenue = Amazon affiliate product boxes. No newsletter.
- Audience: US consumers puzzled by a charge/term/number on their utility bill. 89% organic search (Bing/DuckDuckGo/Yahoo-heavy, almost no Google), 56% mobile / 44% desktop. Sessions are short and question-driven.
- Traffic grew 4.4x in 3 weeks (436 -> 1,925 sessions/30d). Site-wide bounce ~89% is partly question-answer intent (visitor gets answer, leaves) — so time-on-page and multi-page sessions are the real satisfaction signals, bounce alone is not failure.

PRIOR WORK (do not undo, do not repeat)
- Aug-10: the old top-10 pages got the house "Quick Answer" treatment — exemplar pattern: content/blog/what-is-ccf-on-a-water-bill.md.
- TODAY (commit 62e226f9, missions SQ-051..054): a 61-page evidence audit remediated sourcing/facts across the site. Every factual claim currently on disk is freshly evidence-gated. Your job is NOT fact-checking — your lens is the READER EXPERIENCE: intent, structure, momentum, scannability, internal journey, CTA fit.
- HARD RULE: do not propose new factual claims (numbers, dates, laws, product specs, prices). If an improvement genuinely needs one, write NEEDS-VERIFICATION next to it. Rephrasing/restructuring existing verified on-page facts is fine.

HOUSE CONVENTIONS (match them in your Edit Plan)
- "## Quick Answer" = plain markdown H2 immediately after the intro; direct bolded answer in the first sentence.
- Shortcodes: {{< product-box asin="..." label="..." title="..." text="..." >}} (affiliate card, ASIN-keyed, auto-visual), {{< amazon asin="..." text="..." >}} (inline tracked link), {{< faq >}}+{{< faq-schema >}} (end-of-article FAQ), {{< affiliate-disclosure >}}, {{< jump-row >}}, {{< howto >}}/{{< step >}}, {{< visual >}}.
- "Related Reading" bulleted section sits before the FAQ.
- Frontmatter (title/description/slug/draft/aliases) is load-bearing; aliases point consolidated URLs at live pages.

NAVIGATION AIDS
- .squad/content-metrics.json — index of every blog page (path, words, tables, internal-link count, FAQ presence) for finding internal-link targets. Dated 2026-08-28: word counts approximate, verify target existence in content/blog/ before citing.
- AFFILIATE-PLACEMENTS-2026-08-28.md — CTA doctrine: "solve the reader's problem first; the click is a side effect of usefulness"; problem-language anchors ("Diagnose before you spend", "Catch it while it's small"), never product-language.

YOUR ASSIGNED PAGES (Rybbit last-30 baseline, 2026-07-30 to 08-29, pre-change):
- content/blog/23-utility-billing-cycle-explained.md  |  /blog/23-utility-billing-cycle-explained/  |  Rybbit last-30: 59 visits, 65 pv, TOP 55.7s, bounce 83% — decent TOP, high exit: reads then leaves without exploring
- content/blog/07-gas-bill-too-high.md  |  /blog/07-gas-bill-too-high/  |  Rybbit last-30: 56 visits, 63 pv, TOP 92.3s, bounce 84% — longest read of the tier but no journey onward; 4,134 words (longest article of the set)
- content/blog/electric-bill-breakdown-understanding-line-items.md  |  /blog/electric-bill-breakdown-understanding-line-items/  |  Rybbit last-30: 52 visits, 64 pv, TOP 57.7s, bounce 73% — BEST performer of the tier; protect what works, extend the journey

DELIVERABLE — for EACH assigned page write its analysis file with EXACTLY these 9 sections:
1. Intent Model — primary intent, secondary intent, desired outcome, next logical need. Tag every conclusion [RYBBIT] (metric evidence) / [CONTENT] (on-page evidence) / [INFERENCE].
2. First-Screen Verdict — what a mobile visitor (56% of traffic) sees before scrolling; is the primary answer reachable within 2 sentences + one scroll? Name the exact point a reader likely thinks "this isn't giving me what I came for", if any.
3. Gap Analysis — prioritized P0 (kills satisfaction) / P1 (degrades it) / P2 (polish), each citing the specific section/heading where the gap lives.
4. Momentum & Structure — heading usefulness, paragraph bulk, repetition, filler, scannability verdict.
5. Information Gain Plan — concrete additive improvements (worked example, comparison table, FAQ entry, caveat, definition box). Useful-only, zero padding; the site owner rejects artificially-long articles. New facts -> NEEDS-VERIFICATION.
6. Internal Journey — 3 to 8 SPECIFIC links: proposed anchor text + exact target path (verify it exists under content/blog/ first) + placement in the article + why it serves this reader's next need.
7. CTA Fit — the reader's intent stage; existing product boxes / affiliate links on the page: keep / reposition / reframe / replace (with reasoning vs AFFILIATE-PLACEMENTS doctrine); if nothing fits naturally write "NONE - informational" (an acceptable answer).
8. Edit Plan — ordered, concrete, section-level changes: what to change / add / remove, each marked small|medium|large diff. Targeted edits only — never a wholesale rewrite of a working article.
9. Dual Reasoning + Self-Critique — the reader test ("I came here because I need ___" — does the plan satisfy it fast?), the business test (what natural action follows trust?), and what an expert editor would criticize about this plan.

RESULT ENVELOPE (keep <= 60 lines): per assigned page give 5 lines — slug | top P0 gap | headline edit-plan move | # journey links proposed | CTA verdict (keep/reframe/NONE). Full detail lives ONLY in the analysis files.
